nodes.title: 外部参考音频（提示词使用 <Audio 1>）

widgets_values:
[REFERENCE MATERIALS]

@Image 1 is the sole character identity and costume reference for the female protagonist. The portrait, front, back, side, and expression views all depict the same person, not multiple characters. Only one female protagonist may appear in the video. Strictly preserve her dark brown skin, brown eyes, short thick white dreadlocks, blue markings across the eyes and cheeks, pink scarf, white-and-orange futuristic armor, light beige utility pants, single mechanical prosthetic arm, facial identity, body proportions, and costume structure. She does not wear a helmet. Do not mirror the character or switch the prosthetic arm to the opposite side.

@Image 2 is the sole reference for the hovering robot. All views show the same robot, not multiple robots. Only one robot may appear in the video. Strictly preserve its white spherical body, orange armor panels, central cyan glowing eye, two side ducted fans, two small mechanical arms, and rounded proportions.

@Image 3 is the sole environment reference. Strictly preserve the symmetrical industrial corridor constructed from white, orange, and yellow shipping containers. Surveillance cameras and old CRT monitors are mounted along both sides. The monitors display close-up images of human eyes. A massive upward-curving launch ramp stands at the center of the corridor. The top of the ramp aligns with a distant coral-red sun under a bright cyan-blue sky. Keep the corridor structure, perspective, scale, and color relationships stable.

@Image 4 is the sole motorcycle reference. Only one motorcycle may appear in the video. Strictly preserve the white-and-magenta armored body, transparent pink windscreen, cyan LED headlights, cyan illuminated wheel rims, thick treaded tires, exposed black mechanical frame, twin exhaust system, and futuristic off-road racing proportions. Preserve the side number “079” whenever possible. Do not generate any other random letters, distorted text, or fictional brand logos.

@Audio 1 is the sound reference extracted from the target video. The target video must be exactly 8 seconds long. From 0 to 7.08 seconds, closely follow the engine sound, wind, landing impact, metal scraping, acceleration, and airborne timing of @Audio 1. From 7.08 to 8 seconds, naturally extend the final engine tail, high-altitude wind, and airborne whoosh. Do not end in sudden silence. Do not add music or dialogue.

[CORE CONCEPT]

Create an 8-second, 16:9 horizontal, high-quality stylized 3D science-fiction racing game cinematic.

The female protagonist rides the futuristic motorcycle at high speed through the surveillance container corridor. The single hovering robot remains beside her left side throughout the sequence. The motorcycle briefly becomes airborne, lands with a small burst of sparks, continues accelerating toward the massive curved ramp, climbs the ramp, and launches toward the coral-red sun.

Use four clearly defined shots connected by action-matched hard cuts. Maintain continuous direction, speed, character identity, vehicle design, robot design, and spatial continuity across every cut.

[8-SECOND SHOT PLAN]

Shot 1 | 0–1.2 seconds | Frontal low-angle close shot

Position the camera near ground level in the center of the road, using a 24mm wide-angle lens.

The female protagonist leans forward in an aerodynamic riding posture, gripping both handlebars firmly as she rides the motorcycle directly toward the camera at high speed. The cyan LED headlights gradually intensify and create a restrained horizontal lens flare. The front wheel rotates correctly at high speed.

Her white dreadlocks and pink scarf stream backward in the airflow without covering her eyes or face. Her facial identity and blue facial markings remain clear and stable.

The single hovering robot flies steadily outside her left shoulder. Its two ducted fans rotate rapidly. Containers and eye-display monitors rush backward along the corridor perspective. Keep the rider, motorcycle, and robot sharp; apply motion blur only to the wheels and background.

Use an action-matched hard cut when the front wheel approaches the camera.

Shot 2 | 1.2–3.6 seconds | Low-angle side tracking shot

Cut to a low-angle tracking camera on the motorcycle’s left side. The camera travels parallel to the motorcycle at the same speed.

The motorcycle performs one brief and physically believable low jump. The vehicle tilts slightly forward while airborne. The front wheel touches the road first, followed by the rear wheel. On landing, the suspension compresses visibly and rebounds naturally. The underside briefly scrapes the road, producing a small amount of orange-yellow metal sparks.

The rider maintains a professional racing posture: torso lowered, both hands gripping the handlebars, and both feet correctly positioned on the foot pegs. Her body responds naturally to the suspension compression.

The robot follows slightly above and behind the motorcycle on the rider’s left side. It must not block the rider or collide with the vehicle.

The exhaust and taillights create short, concentrated cyan and magenta energy trails. Do not turn these trails into large clouds of colored smoke. The containers, surveillance cameras, and eye monitors move rapidly backward. Apply realistic background motion blur while keeping the rider, motorcycle, and robot clearly defined.

Hard cut when the motorcycle has fully landed and accelerates again.

Shot 3 | 3.6–5.2 seconds | Rear low-angle chase shot

Move the camera to a low position directly behind the motorcycle and follow it along the central axis of the container corridor.

The motorcycle accelerates toward the massive curved ramp in the distance. The top of the ramp remains vertically aligned with the coral-red sun.

The rider leans farther forward as she accelerates. Her pink scarf streams steadily behind her. The robot maintains a fixed escort position on the motorcycle’s left side.

Keep both sides of the container corridor symmetrical. The eye-display monitors pass rapidly in perspective. Each monitor may show only a single close-up human eye. Do not show complete faces, letters, subtitles, or corrupted text on the screens.

As the engine pitch rises, gradually intensify the short cyan and magenta exhaust trails. Keep the camera centered on the road. Do not sway left and right or orbit around the motorcycle.

Use an action-matched hard cut when the motorcycle reaches the bottom of the ramp.

Shot 4 | 5.2–8 seconds | Wide rear chase, ramp climb, and airborne finish

Cut to a slightly more distant wide rear-following shot that clearly shows the motorcycle, rider, robot, and massive curved ramp.

From 5.2 to 6.5 seconds, the motorcycle climbs rapidly along the center of the ramp. Both wheels must remain correctly attached to the curved road surface. The engine power increases, and the twin exhaust outlets produce two short, concentrated cyan-and-magenta propulsion trails.

The rider lowers her body farther in response to the slope. Her hands and feet remain correctly attached to the controls. The robot climbs beside her on the left, maintaining a stable distance.

From 6.5 to 7.2 seconds, the motorcycle reaches the crest. The front wheel rises naturally, and the entire vehicle launches forward along the direction of the ramp. The robot becomes airborne at the same time. The rider, motorcycle, and robot form a clear silhouette against the coral-red sun.

From 7.2 to 8 seconds, extend the heroic airborne ending. The motorcycle continues moving slowly upward and forward instead of freezing in midair. The camera pulls back slightly so that the complete rider, motorcycle, and robot move into the center of the red sun. The scarf and exhaust trails continue flowing backward. The engine tail and high-altitude wind gradually diminish.

Hold the stable airborne composition for the final 0.25 seconds. Do not cut to black, freeze abruptly, make the subjects disappear, or let them leave the frame. End with the motorcycle continuing its flight into the sky.

[VISUAL STYLE]

High-quality stylized 3D science-fiction game cinematic. The image should feel bright, clean, energetic, and saturated without excessive glow.

Use a controlled palette of cyan-blue, white, orange, magenta, and coral red.

Render the protagonist’s skin with a natural matte finish and subtle texture. Clearly distinguish the materials of painted armor, composite panels, transparent windscreen, mechanical metal, rubber tires, and exposed vehicle components. Preserve subtle wear, seams, construction details, and industrial scale on the shipping containers.

Use restrained wheel motion blur, background motion blur, lens flare, and small metal sparks. Keep the protagonist’s face, the motorcycle body, and the robot sharp and recognizable.

Avoid cheap neon lighting, excessive bloom, particle clutter, plastic-looking materials, oversharpening, or obvious AI-generated artifacts.

[CAMERA AND EDITING]

Use four shots in this exact order:

Frontal low-angle close shot → low-angle side tracking shot → rear low-angle chase shot → wide rear ramp-climb and airborne shot.

Connect all shots with action-matched hard cuts. Preserve the riding direction, speed, rider position, motorcycle design, robot position, and spatial continuity across every cut.

Do not use unnecessary camera orbits, random zooms, handheld shaking, reverse motion, axis jumps, excessive camera rotation, slow motion, dissolves, fades, or transformation transitions.

The motorcycle must always travel forward through the corridor toward the ramp and the sun.

[SOUND]

Use @Audio 1 as the primary sound and timing reference.

The motorcycle engine rises continuously with speed. The landing includes a short suspension impact, tire contact, and restrained metal scraping sound. The straight acceleration section includes high-speed wind and the robot’s ducted-fan sound. The engine reaches a higher pitch during the ramp climb. Add a brief aerodynamic whoosh at the moment of takeoff.

From 7.08 to 8 seconds, naturally extend the final engine tail, wind, and airborne whoosh, then let them resolve smoothly at exactly 8 seconds.

No dialogue, no added background music, and no explosion sounds.

[CRITICAL RESTRICTIONS]

Only one female protagonist, one motorcycle, and one hovering robot may appear. Do not interpret the multi-view reference sheets as multiple subjects.

Preserve the protagonist’s facial identity, skin tone, white dreadlocks, blue facial markings, pink scarf, costume structure, body proportions, and prosthetic-arm placement. Do not mirror the character, switch the prosthetic arm, alter the face, change the costume, add a helmet, create extra limbs, detach the hands from the handlebars, or detach the feet from the foot pegs.

Preserve the motorcycle’s frame, wheels, windscreen, headlights, exhausts, armor, colors, and proportions. Do not deform the wheels, turn the tires oval, melt the frame, change the number of wheels, merge the rider with the motorcycle, make the vehicle penetrate the road, or make it float without physical cause.

Preserve the robot’s single central eye, two ducted fans, two mechanical arms, spherical body, colors, and scale. Do not duplicate the robot, add extra fans or limbs, melt its body, make it disappear, or let it collide with the rider.

Do not add vehicles, pedestrians, weapons, explosions, road obstacles, buildings, readable text, subtitles, logos, or watermarks.

Do not generate corrupted text or complete human faces on the monitors. Do not bend or melt the ramp, float the containers, flicker the sun, change the sun’s size, or transform the sun into a portal, black hole, or explosion.
